classes.name: Triptans
classes.description: Acute migraine 5-HT1B/1D agonists: sumatriptan (tablet, nasal, injection; Imitrex, Tosymra, Zembrace), rizatriptan (Maxalt, MLT), zolmitriptan (Zomig), eletriptan (Relpax), naratriptan, almotriptan, frovatriptan, sumatriptan/naproxen (Treximet).
classes.plainDescription: A pill (or spray/shot) taken when a migraine starts.

classes.name: Acute CGRP antagonists (gepants) & ditans
classes.description: Acute CGRP receptor antagonists and ditans: rimegepant (Nurtec ODT, also preventive), ubrogepant (Ubrelvy), zavegepant nasal (Zavzpret), lasmiditan (Reyvow).
classes.plainDescription: A newer migraine pill (or nasal spray) for when triptans don't work or aren't safe.

classes.name: CGRP preventives

records.verificationNote: Searched rimegepant, Nurtec, ubrogepant, Ubrelvy, zavegepant, Zavzpret, lasmiditan, Reyvow: no match. Absence not treated as confirmed exclusion. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: PDL wording read as one consistent whole: it is a preferred-drug list, not a full list (p.1: "All Georgia Medicaid drugs are covered by CareSource. This is just a list of preferred drugs." and "It is also not meant to be a full list."); the "closed formulary" sentence (p.3: "If a drug is not listed, a formulary exception may be asked for coverage") is boilerplate and is not used to infer exclusions. A drug absent from the list is therefore unconfirmed, not excluded: it is covered if Georgia Medicaid covers it, likely through PA or exception review. Context only, not cited as a source: the Georgia Medicaid FFS PDL eff. 10/1/2026 lists Nurtec ODT and Ubrelvy as preferred with PA, so Georgia Medicaid covers them even though CareSource's PDL omits them.]
